_meta.description: branch_uid -> {lat, lon, city, method} or null (unresolved, awaiting review - never a guess). method is one of: nominatim (branch's own address, first or cleanup pass - see first_pass/second_pass below), cheapersal (third-party exact-address fill, third_pass below). Precedence highest first: first-pass geocode, cleanup-pass geocode, cheapersal exact-address fill, otherwise null.

first_pass.description: KAN-34 first pass: every branch's own Address/City queried against OSM Nominatim.

_meta.keys: Keyed by our generated branch_uid. chain_id and store_id are the raw key this uuid was assigned to - the same pair that forms the stores table's primary key, after split_id() and stripping the store id's leading zeros - so the file can be read without data/branch_ids.json beside it. A row with precision null has no coordinate.
_meta.precision: 'address' means the point is the branch's own address and may be used for distance. 'city' means the geocoder could only place the locality - the point is the town, not the shop - so it may filter by city but must never measure a distance. A null entry has no coordinate at all.

second_pass.description: KAN-34 cleanup pass: cleaned address (and, for some, street+house-number only) re-queried for every branch the first pass left as no_result. See review/geocode_review.md for which rule recovered each.

sources.cheapersal: third-party snapshot, filled only on exact address + city agreement
sources.google: Google Geocoding, one hand-run of 557 requests against a 1,000 ceiling

third_pass.description: KAN-34 cheapersal fill: exact-address match (after meaning-preserving normalisation only) against the third-party cheapersal store list, for branches still unresolved after both geocoding passes. Also carries the post-fill sanity check that nulls any geocode more than 20km from a known store in its own city, or outside Israel.
